# Video script: Refer or not?

> DRAFT - NOT FOR CLINICAL USE. Contains claims with status 'ai-extracted' that no clinician has verified.

Unit D11 | Target length: 5 min

| # | Shot | Narration | Claims |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Presenter to camera | You do not need a diagnosis to refer. A suspicion is enough. | IS23-078 |
| 2 | Graphic: list of fetal indications appearing one by one | Examples from the scan: a suspected structural heart anomaly; an anomaly outside the heart that is known to go with heart disease; suspected poor function or a large heart; hydrops; a rate that stays at one-ten or below, or at one-eighty or above; a frequent or persistently irregular rhythm; a nuchal translucency of three and a half millimetres or more. | IS23-082 |
| 3 | Graphic: list of maternal and family indications | Examples from the history: congenital heart disease in a parent, sibling or half-sibling of this fetus; diabetes before pregnancy; anti-Ro antibodies. The full list is in the unit. | IS23-083 |
| 4 | Graphic: 'not enough evidence' list | Some factors, taken alone, lack enough evidence of a clearly raised risk: an isolated bright spot in the heart, a single umbilical artery on its own, soft markers for aneuploidy outside the heart. A suspicious screen still counts, whatever the history. | IS23-085, IS23-078 |
| 5 | Presenter | A high proportion of detectable heart disease is in pregnancies with no risk factor. Quality screening of every pregnancy, and timely referral, are what matter. | IS23-080 |
